papers.title: Hot or Cold? Adaptive Temperature Sampling for Code Generation with Large Language Models
papers.why: per-token temperature at code-block starts judged on pass@k; no counterfactually located decision token, no committed dose prediction, no algorithm-choice outcome; our A6 arm implements its rule (T 2 at block starts, T 1 elsewhere)
papers.quote: hard-to-predict tokens ... mostly appear at the start of a code block

papers.title: EDT: Improving Large Language Models' Generation by Entropy-based Dynamic Temperature Sampling
papers.why: temperature chosen per step from the next-token entropy; position chosen by entropy, not by a counterfactual locator; our A5 (threshold EDT) and A7 (entropy-max at matched dose) arms
papers.quote: a better balance between generation quality and diversity by choosing the temperature parameter dynamically

papers.title: Control the Temperature: Selective Sampling for Diverse and High-Quality LLM Outputs
papers.why: learned risk score switches greedy vs high-T per token for math reasoning; risk avoidance, not dosed idea mixing at a located fork
papers.quote: switches between greedy and high-temperature sampling based on a sampling risk metric

papers.title: Exploring Multi-Temperature Strategies for Token- and Rollout-Level Control in RLVR
papers.why: higher T on high-entropy reasoning tokens during RL training; training-time exploration, entropy-defined positions
papers.quote: Higher temperatures are used for reasoning tokens to encourage exploration

papers.title: Beyond the 80/20 Rule: High-Entropy Minority Tokens Drive Effective Reinforcement Learning for LLM Reasoning
papers.why: high-entropy forking tokens in CoT; RL gradient restriction plus a note that raising their temperature helps; entropy-located, not counterfactually located, and not about algorithm choice
papers.quote: these tokens semantically act as critical forks that steer the model toward diverse reasoning pathways

papers.title: Forking Paths in Neural Text Generation
papers.why: resampling-based forking-token detection with change-point statistics, the basis of our Stage 1 locator; it does not dose temperature at the located token
papers.quote: LLMs are often just a single token away from saying something very different

papers.title: Forking Fast: Efficiently Estimating Uncertainty Dynamics in Text Generation
papers.why: cheaper estimation of forking points by TVD between outcome distributions; locating, not intervening
papers.quote: Forking points are defined as points t such that TVD(o_t, o_{t+N}) > epsilon

papers.title: Embarrassingly Simple Self-Distillation Improves Code Generation
papers.why: fork vs lock positions and why one global temperature is a compromise; fixes it by self-distillation, not by dosing a located token
papers.quote: Locks are positions where syntax demands a single dominant token, and forks are positions where several continuations are valid

papers.title: Turning Up the Heat: Min-p Sampling for Creative and Coherent LLM Outputs
papers.why: the coherent high-temperature truncation sampler; our A4 arm (min-p 0.1 at T 3.0, temperature last)
papers.quote: a dynamic truncation method ... threshold scales with the top token's probability

summary: No retrieved work applies temperature only at a counterfactually located decision token with a dose committed from that token's logits and scores the algorithm mix; AdapT (block starts) and EDT/80-20 (entropy) are the nearest per-token-temperature rivals and are run here as A6, A5 and A7.
